questions.explain: Arc rests on two components: the Connected Machine Agent (outbound HTTPS 443, no inbound firewall rules) and the Arc SQL Server extension, which projects the instance into ARM as Microsoft.AzureArcData/sqlServerInstances for unified monitoring, policy, and security.
options: The SQL Server Data Tools agent and a VPN tunnel
The Connected Machine Agent and the Arc SQL Server extension, projecting the instance into ARM
questions.q: Which two components make up Azure Arc-Enabled SQL Server's architecture?

questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: Arc does not move data, does not replicate databases to Azure, and does not change how SQL Server operates internally — the agent has read-only access to metadata and cannot execute DML or DDL.
options: It migrates the databases to Azure SQL
It does not move or replicate data — the agent has read-only metadata access and cannot execute DML or DDL
questions.q: What does Azure Arc NOT do to your on-premises SQL Server, per the chapter?

questions.explain: Extended Security Updates through Arc are a significant benefit: Microsoft provides ESU patches free of charge for Arc-connected instances (2012/2014), subject to Software Assurance or Azure subscription conditions — often justifying onboarding alone.
options: It is never a valid strategy
It provides free Extended Security Updates for Arc-connected 2012/2014 instances
It removes the need for backups
questions.q: Why does the chapter say Arc alone can justify onboarding for shops still running SQL Server 2012/2014?

questions.explain: Defender for SQL does two things: vulnerability assessment (scans config for known misconfigurations like sa enabled, xp_cmdshell exposed, TRUSTWORTHY ON) and advanced threat protection (analyzes audit logs for behavioral anomalies like SQL injection and brute-force).
options: Vulnerability assessment of configuration plus advanced threat protection from audit-log behavioral analysis
questions.q: What are the two functions of Microsoft Defender for SQL on Arc instances?

questions.explain: Arc tracks license type per instance: LicenseIncluded, PAYG, or Paid (Azure Hybrid Benefit). Setting it incorrectly leads to billing surprises or compliance gaps.
options: LicenseIncluded, PAYG, or Paid (Azure Hybrid Benefit)
questions.q: What license-type options does Arc track for each SQL Server instance?
